title: Standards and common protocols
sub: Worksheet for the 360° experience: Protocol city
objectives: understand the need for standards in computing
understand the seven common protocols and what they are used for
starter: List every acronym you already associate with the internet. Which ones do you think are rules for sending data, and which are something else?

stations.name: Standards
stations.challenge: What would happen if every phone maker used a different charging connector?

logic.title: Why are standards needed in computing?
Which of these is a standard?

stations.name: Protocols
stations.challenge: What is the difference between a standard and a protocol?

logic.title: Why must both devices use the same protocol?

stations.name: Web protocols
stations.fact: HTTP is used for... HTTPS adds...
stations.challenge: Why should a shopping website use HTTPS rather than HTTP?

logic.title: What does HTTPS add to HTTP?

stations.name: Email protocols
stations.challenge: Why is IMAP better than POP if you read email on a phone and a laptop?

logic.title: Which protocol keeps your emails in sync across your phone and laptop?

stations.name: FTP
stations.challenge: A web designer has finished a site. Which protocol might they use to put it on the web server?

logic.title: Which protocol would upload a website's files to a web server?

stations.name: TCP/IP
stations.challenge: What would happen to a web page if some packets went missing and nothing checked?

final.title: Final challenge: protocol match

exam: Explain why agreed standards matter when devices from different makers connect.
Name the protocol used to send email to a mail server.
Describe what HTTPS adds to HTTP and why it matters.
Explain how TCP and IP work together when a web page is requested.
confidence: The common protocols and what they do
The difference between standards and protocols
